pillar_reactions.evidence: He arrived pre-sold and volunteered the mechanism himself before the rep presented anything: 'I know that kettlebells that I've been noticing, your mobility still, it pretty much gets enhanced because of the movements and all that. So that's another reason why I kind of like chose this, especially with the tightness and the pain that I have like on my shoulder.' He already owns kettlebells and had been following Trevor's social media: 'I like what this guy's talking about... he talks about how exercising in this matter could help you be pain-free, gain strength, and stay able to be mobile.' Tied directly to his own goal, unprompted.

Presented briefly and generically — eat for health, micronutrients, protein, sustainable — with a one-line nod to his vegetarianism. He had to raise his own dietary constraint twice before it was properly addressed, then asked the mechanics question directly: 'as far as nutrition wise, you know, I kind of did say, that I was vegetarian. Have you guys worked with a person that has been vegetarian before?' The reassurance satisfied him ('That's really good to hear') but was delivered via an unprompted generalisation about Indian genetics rather than any description of how vegetarian programming actually works.

This was the pillar he came for — he named it before the rep presented anything: 'I also want to have some type of accountability, something where I can know that I have somebody watching over me in that situation, kind of like when I was in physical therapy where I had my physical therapist.' Delivered as 24/7 Trevor access, weekly in-app check-ins, form video review and 'we're holding you to the best version of Luis. We're not holding you to the guy you are now.' He then probed the delivery mechanism — 'how would that take place, like through Zoom calls?' — and pushed again on whether plans arrive in the app. Understood and bought, but with a live reservation about the absence of synchronous contact.

anchors.raw: I was not expecting 6k, but I was expecting someone, I know above 3k easy
anchors.note: He arrived anchored at roughly half the list price and said so plainly. The gap closed because belief had already been established in phase 6, not because the anchor was ever addressed — the rep never asked where the sub-$4k expectation came from, which would have been worth knowing given the setter had already spoken to him.

anchors.raw: I could put it in the credit card, but right now, like I owe some things that I got to pay off
anchors.note: A liquidity constraint rather than an income one. It was resolved by splitting the payment and then by offering Klarna, so the deal closed by adding a second financing instrument on top of an already-disclosed card balance. No cash-on-hand, monthly-surplus or available-credit figures were ever taken, so nobody involved knows whether the 90-day balance is serviceable.

anchors.raw: I could go online, search a little, search for something with kettlebell exercise. And then I'll have some type of setup, right?
anchors.note: Present as an anchor but already self-disqualified before the rep touched it: 'it's not like that one-on-one or it's not like somebody was telling me like, oh, you're doing it correct.' He had run the substitute, found the gap himself, and named it as coaching and feedback. The cheapest deal in the batch to defend, and it needed no defending.

anchors.raw: kind of like when I was in physical therapy where I had my physical therapist, I was able to rely on, kind of like get feedback from them... I remained in contact with them throughout a good period
anchors.note: The single strongest supportive anchor on the call. He has a lived, positive template for paying an expert to supervise his body and explicitly wants this to be the same thing — he later closed the loop himself on the education pillar: 'Just like how physical therapy was for me in that period of time.' Worth noting for positioning generally, and worth noting for risk: he is buying this as a continuation of clinical care.

unmet_demand.want: Synchronous coaching contact — video or face-to-face calls with his coach, modelled on the physiotherapist relationship he valued
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The product deliberately does not include calls. The rep was explicit: 'we have an app, we don't do any calls, we don't really, we found that we used to, but we don't really need them, and it ended up just being a waste of time.' He substituted 24/7 asynchronous voice notes and an off-menu personal offer to jump on monthly himself. The prospect asked for this twice, before and after the pitch, so it is a settled preference rather than a passing question.

unmet_demand.want: Training that rehabilitates rather than aggravates post-traumatic cervical, left-shoulder and upper-back injury with active pain and documented compensation patterns
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The offer asserts it does this — 'we'll get you out of the pain', 'get rid of the imbalances and compensations, get rid of the pain' — but nothing on the call establishes that a programme built on swings and snatches is appropriate for this injury history, and no clinician was consulted or asked about. The prospect is buying pain relief on the rep's assurance alone.

Actually served — the company reports many vegetarian clients. Recorded only because the prospect had to raise it three times before getting an answer, and the answer he got was about genetics rather than about the programming.
